title: Nonlinear Mutual-Information Bound for Side-Channel Queries
summary: Mutual information is at most the logarithm of the secret-space size, so the linear-in-query bound is not tight for large query counts; a practical bounded nonlinear bound remains open.

formal_statement.body: For a secret $K$ observed through side-channel leakage $Y$ over $q$ queries, a known upper bound on $I(K;Y)$ grows linearly with $q$, although $I(K;Y)\leq\log|K|$, so the linear bound cannot be tight for large $q$. Derive an alternative practical upper bound that depends nonlinearly on $q$ and remains bounded as $q$ increases.

scope.domain: Information-theoretic analysis of side-channel leakage across multiple queries.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Derive a practical upper bound on I(K;Y) that is nonlinear in q and remains bounded as q grows.

citations.label: Formal Security Proofs via Doeblin Coefficients: Optimal Side-channel Factorization from Noisy Leakage to Random Probing

progress.summary: The source contrasts the known linear-in-query mutual-information bound with the fixed information-theoretic cap and explicitly leaves a practical bounded nonlinear alternative as an open question. It does not provide the requested mutual-information bound.
citation_labels: Julien Béguinot et al., Formal Security Proofs via Doeblin Coefficients: Optimal Side-channel Factorization from Noisy Leakage to Random Probing
